qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High switching costs in core cloud HCM and Financial Management database of record, but excessive stock-based compensation (SBC) dilutes economic returns, failing the 12% ROIC proof-of-moat test.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (REJECT). Proof of moat fails: massive stock-based compensation (SBC) has kept 5-year median GAAP ROIC deeply sub-hurdle (-5.4%), failing the Gate 3b 12% hurdle. In addition, its per-employee seat pricing is directly exposed to AI-driven enterprise headcount reductions (Macrotrend #1). Downstream gates bypassed per waterfall.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is -5.4% (reported median ROIC ~1.8%) due to persistent heavy stock-based compensation (~18-20% of revenues) diluting real economic owner returns. While non-GAAP operating margins appear respectable (~25%), true owner economic profits fail the 12% hurdle. Core HCM model charges per employee seat, leaving terminal pricing power highly vulnerable to agentic AI enterprise headcount contraction.
